findings.title: Rejected device is cached before the limit check, allowing it to bypass the limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache via SetDefault before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. If CreateOrUpdateDevice then returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains, so the anonymous client's next request from the same device hits the cache at line 83, TagDevice returns nil, and Authenticate grants access even though the device was never admitted. The limit is therefore only enforced for the first attempt within the 29-minute cache TTL. The cache entry must only be set after a successful store, or deleted on error.

findings.title: Device-limit enforcement has a count-then-insert race that admits devices beyond the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices and then, in a separate DB session, inserts the new device if count < deviceLimit. There is no transaction, lock, or unique admission constraint tying the count to the insert, so two (or more) concurrent first-time requests on the same or different Grafana instances can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. Under a burst of new anonymous devices the limit is not reliably enforced.

findings.title: Provider signature changed without updating Wire-generated dependency injection
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore and constructs the store itself via ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit) (line 43), and ProvideAnonDBStore itself now requires an int64. The checked-in Wire injector (pkg/server/wire_gen.go and the anonymous WireSet) is not updated in this PR, so it still passes an AnonStore to this constructor and cannot supply the new int64 argument to ProvideAnonDBStore; the server package will fail to compile / wire generation will fail until the injector is regenerated and updated.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication is now synchronously blocked on device-store database calls
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout context; it now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context. Every cache-miss anonymous request now waits on a COUNT query plus an INSERT/UPDATE (and, when at the limit, a second UPDATE) before an identity is returned, so slow or contended database calls directly add latency to, or stall until request cancellation, all anonymous page/API loads. Only ErrDeviceLimitReached needs to be decided synchronously; the previous decoupling for ordinary tagging latency has been removed.

findings.title: updateDevice uses generic '?' placeholders unlike the Postgres-specific upsert path
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice carefully uses $1..$5 placeholders for Postgres in its INSERT ... ON CONFLICT statement, but the new updateDevice (used for every request once the limit is reached) hardcodes '?' placeholders. On Postgres deployments this UPDATE will fail with a syntax/placeholder error instead of updating an already-admitted device, so existing anonymous devices are rejected with a database error as soon as the limit is reached, while SQLite/MySQL continue to work. The update statement needs dialect-specific placeholders like the insert path.
